body:
CANONICAL: day-to-day landing practice in Engram (Engram::Fable; rev 8, 2026-10-25, corrects the focus lesson now that w-d9af has landed at 5160c093; rev 7 trimmed history and updated LANDING ORDER to the carry model at d800d17f; older wording is in rev 6). These are coordinator practices and lessons, not Greg's words unless quoted; they add no gate or authority beyond the checked-in rules.

WORKTREES. Put parallel worktrees at .worktrees/NAME inside the checkout (ignored by Git); TermAl refuses reviewer delegations outside the project. Build each in its own target/ (leave CARGO_TARGET_DIR unset). Scratch goes under target/ of the tree you work in; create no new folder in the main root, since an unignored folder drifts the freeze and voids a running gate. A gate on one worktree never covers another: after moving a patch onto a new master (saved patch, fast-forward only, never a rebase without Greg's word), run the checks its file types need and freeze again. After landing and done, the lander runs `cargo clean -q` in its own worktree. Never `git worktree remove` while an OPEN item still cites its runs: review-runs live under .git/worktrees/NAME and go with it, so copy cited runs into .evidence first (rules-post-completion-cleanup). Record the numbers an evaluator needs in a note.

LANDING ORDER (see rules-merger-role and rules-greg-merge-focus). The Engram merger (session-14575 since 2026-10-25) integrates and lands one integration at a time, with ONE full gate host-wide through Termal::Fable2's slot. Coders send one complete READY package each.
- When master moves under a reviewed package, the Merger carries it under `/review-changes` section 6a (landed at d800d17f). A clean carry adopts the Coder's completed review, with no fresh pair for base movement alone; the final integration still gets its exact-tree gate. Conflicts or changed content go back to the Coder.
- A gate binds the exact final tree: land Markdown or authority changes BEFORE gating a code batch that will sit on them.
- Independent acceptance evaluation is enabled for Engram by Greg's newer word (Asistant #748, 2026-11-09; rules-greg-evaluation-on-engram-2026-11-09), superseding the earlier deferral. Record a criterion-to-evidence map that claims no more than the evidence shows, obtain the required independent evaluation on its current basis, and complete only on a fresh pass. Criteria that require landing or live operation retain their actual dependency; evaluation does not replace review or gate requirements.
- Reviewer briefs require memory recovery BEFORE inspection (rules-merger-role r16).

GATES. Stop or discard a running gate before editing its input. Fix-round step 1, before opening any file: for a detached launcher run, end its executor's process tree (the pid from the launch output, after confirming its command line names the run), run `node scripts/test-launcher.mjs recover RUN_DIR`, then edit and freeze again. Classify every gate failure (test or environment defect, product defect) and act in the same session; never normalise a retry.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA must be provable from what the independent evaluator can read: the repository at the evaluated source, the item's own holder notes and typed evidence, and the host brief. Not from project memory, another item, a non-holder's note or tracker reads. Housekeeping such as revising a memory belongs in notes, not criteria.

FOCUS AND HOST-OBSERVED TESTS (behaviour since 5160c093, w-d9af). A SUCCESSFUL note, update, gate or claim given another held item's ref moves the session's focus to that item, and the next turn is bound to it. A REFUSED mutation leaves the prior focus, or no focus, unchanged; read-only show never navigates. So name the target explicitly (for example `accept` with its work_ref) rather than relying on ambient focus after a refusal. Claim the item as the LAST work mutation of a turn, run the test in the next turn in that item's root, and check the store after that turn ends.

TOOLS. In PowerShell, give .NET file APIs absolute paths, because Set-Location doesn't change what .NET resolves against. Prefer the Edit and Write tools.

INSTALL NOTICE TO TERMAL. Every landing installs a new binary, even a docs-only one, because the revision is embedded. After verifying each landing, tell Termal::Fable2 the commit, the full build_fingerprint, the installed exe sha256 and whether the behaviour changed. Warn a pinned TermAl live check before the next Engram landing.

MEASUREMENTS PIN A COPY. A timing or behaviour measurement that must name its producer copies the installed engram.exe ONCE into its own worktree's target/, records the copy's sha256 and build_fingerprint, and uses that copy for every sample; never blend producers. Warn a running measurer before a landing.

DISK. Implementers never clean another session's worktree. The coordinator may remove target/debug only from STALE worktrees (no build for hours, no active owner), after checking each absolute path is inside the repository and ends in .worktrees/NAME/target/debug. Source, target/tmp and review-runs stay. When C falls below about 20 GB free, sweep before a landing. Failures during disk-full are environment defects.

TERMAL STRICT READERS (Fable2, ebe242f7 #508). TermAl parses three Engram outputs with deny_unknown_fields: the binding-evidence page, named_root_sighting_read, and the control-policy receipt's `acceptance_evaluation` object. Any added, renamed or removed field there is a live-consumer change: flag it to the TermAl coordinator and land only once TermAl's reader is ready. show, next and refusal readers are non-strict.

WORKTREE REMOVAL AFTER CLOSE (Greg, Advisor #929). After a verified landing and done, with no live claim, carried gate or review, or required artifact, the lander runs `git worktree remove <path>` WITHOUT --force, after checking the path is under .worktrees\. Dirty or unmerged worktrees are never removed. Removal doesn't yet free TermAl's named-root entry (TermAl w-a938c2757bba).

2026-11-10 lesson (w-92f8): when an audited authority change is carried onto a moved master, the AUDITING coordinator's carry identity audit (/review-changes "When an audited authority change is carried onto a new base") must be recorded on the item BEFORE landing. A coordinator note that the change was "applied unchanged", and even byte-identical governing blobs, do not replace it. 885c032e landed without it; the after-landing audit passed and Greg approved closure („tak”, Asistant #854), but criterion 3 had to be revised to record the deviation.
